surface-sunken.$description: A terminal suns its rows into the phosphor floor: one step below the page, still a surface.

surface-raised.$description: A raised panel steps one lightness up from the page and wears the ring; on black, a shadow alone would not separate it.

semantic.$description: Status colors. Named by meaning, never by hue.

error.$description: Error status, same value as danger.

link.$description: A second hue for links; the primary is reserved for the phosphor fill.

field.$description: A field's own surface. In a terminal palette a field is sunk rather than raised, so its surface is darker than the page.

border-strong.$description: A control's own edge: stronger than border, which divides content.

scrim.$description: The page dims into the terminal's own black. A neutral grey scrim would read as a panel from another machine.

on-accent.$description: Text on an accent fill. Derived: console's accents are bright, so ink reads and white does not.

on-semantic-error.$description: Text on the matching fill. A fill with no foreground cannot be read, which is what this token prevents.

on-danger.$description: The legacy name for the ink on the error fill. It points at `color.on-semantic-error` — the role the contract requires, the floor is measured on, and the danger button and the danger badge wear — so the two names can never disagree.

on-semantic-info.$description: Text on the matching fill. A fill with no foreground cannot be read, which is what this token prevents.

on-secondary.$description: Text on the matching fill. A fill with no foreground cannot be read, which is what this token prevents.

disabled.$description: The fill a dead control wears: one step up from the terminal floor, in the terminal's own blue-grey. A control that cannot be pressed still occupies its cell.

on-disabled.$description: The ink on that fill: the muted phosphor, dim enough to recede and bright enough to read.

spacing.$description: The spacing scale. Every gap, pad and inset is one of these steps.

font.$description: Typography: which face, how large, how heavy, and how open the tracking sits. Console is monospaced only where a terminal speaks in fixed width.

sans.$description: A proportional face for the interface. A terminal keeps its voice in the mono face below — code, markup, readouts — and not in every heading and paragraph, where monospace reads as shouting.

heading.$value: JetBrains Mono, ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace
heading.$description: Terminal voice: the mono is the heading.

body.$description: The body face: the same interface face, named so the surface is whole.

brand.$description: The logotype face — one brand, every starter.

letter-spacing.$description: How far the letters sit from each other. A monospace face has already made every glyph the same width, so tracking here does not open a word up so much as hold a column header apart from the text under it.

tighter.$description: Rarely right in a terminal. Named because a fixed-width grid is exactly where a runaway negative step shows: the columns stop lining up.

tight.$description: A long fixed-width line, where the last character needs to come back inside the viewport.

normal.$description: Everything a terminal prints. Zero is the honest answer: the face's own advance width is the layout.

wide.$description: A field label or a panel title, where the heading has to be findable by scanning rather than reading.

wider.$description: A section rule of text. At a fixed advance width the air lands between the columns, which is where a terminal wants it.

widest.$description: The one-word banner. Past this a fixed-width cell stops reading as a character grid and starts reading as a poster.

radius.$description: Corner rounding, from square to fully round.

opacity.$description: How much of a thing is shown, as a fraction. The fractions themselves are the same in every theme, but console is dark-only and its foregrounds are bright: on black a fraction reads dimmer at the same number than it would on white, so the low steps are spent carefully here.

10.$description: A ghost. On a dark surface this is already below the threshold phosphor glow, so it is for decoration only.

20.$description: Disabled. Bright text over black survives a long way down, so this is as dim as a label can go and still be read.

30.$description: A disabled command the reader may still want to see in the list they are scanning.

40.$description: The dimmed step: an empty progress track, an unfilled meter.

50.$description: Half. The step most rules ask for, and the one a theme is most likely to have an opinion about.

60.$description: Muted but still read: a hint line the reader is expected to act on.

70.$description: Secondary output, such as a comment, that must stay legible against the black.

80.$description: A hair under full strength, for a line that should read as output rather than as emphasis.

90.$description: Almost opaque: a scrim over the terminal behind a dialog, dimmed without looking black.

100.$description: Fully shown. Named so a rule can say it rather than assume it.

shadow.$description: Elevation: a phosphor ring, and the dark offset that grounds it. Three steps on purpose — a component that needs a more specific edge states it, and a step nothing spends stops being a step.

breakpoint.$description: Viewport widths where layout steps change.

z-index.$description: Stacking order. Layer, never a magic number at the call site.

motion.$description: How things move and how long it takes. A terminal snaps: the phosphor answers and is done, and nothing drifts.

loop.$description: The period of an endless animation: the skeleton's pulse and the loop utilities. A cursor's blink, not a blink of light.

$description: Terminal phosphor, ported from sail. Dark-only green-on-black.

button.$description: Component tokens: the decisions a theme owns for its buttons. Metrics that every theme would answer the same way are spent in the CSS instead.

border.$description: Stroke weight. Every control and surface reads `width`, so a theme changes its edge weight in one place; this theme's ladder is in whole pixels, because a terminal that renders a hairline at 1.5px has stopped being a terminal.

width.$description: The cell grid. Every box in a terminal is one pixel of phosphor, and it is also the theme's focus ring, so the grid and the selection state are the same width.

width-2.$description: The selected edge: two cells, the width a highlighted row reads as.

width-4.$description: The heavy edge. Reserved for the one frame on screen that owns the terminal, such as the active pane.

width-8.$description: A drawn block rather than an outlined one. Almost never right here, and named so the decision is explicit when it is taken.

focus.$description: The focus ring, shared by every interactive element: buttons, links, fields, summaries and dialogs.

icon.$description: Glyph sizes, from the reader's own root rather than the element they sit in — a step has to be a jump, and an `em` step against 14px prose is 2px.

badge.$description: Component tokens: the decisions a theme owns for its badges. Metrics that every theme would answer the same way are spent in the CSS instead.

edge.$description: The stroke the badge draws around itself, so a small shape holds apart from the page. Zero leaves it a bare fill with no edge.

pill.$description: Fully round reads as a pill; false squares it into a tag.

checkbox.$description: How physical a checkbox is: one scalar driving three inset shadows. Zero is flat and drawn.

switch.$description: How physical a switch is. A terminal switch is a filled pill, not a lit surface.

avatar.$description: How big an avatar is, in the type ladder a terminal thinks in. A console avatar is a glyph box, not a photograph.

sm.$description: The size for a face in a list or a comment: it reads beside its label without leading the row.

md.$description: The default: a face beside a name, or a profile header at rest.

lg.$description: A face as the subject of a page: a profile header at the top of a long column.

card.$description: The card's own decisions: its corner, the air inside it, the ink of its edge, and the elevation it rests at. A card is not a button, and need not round the same way.

radius.$description: Three pixels: a terminal rounds its boxes by a hair, never by a lot.

padding.$description: The air inside the card, between its parts and around its edge.

border.$description: The ink of the card's own edge: the page's hairline, because a rule is all that separates one thing from the next here.

elevation.$description: The phosphor ring and the dark offset: a panel is a panel, and on black it has to say so.

alert.$description: The alert's own decisions: its corner, the air around its message, and the ink of the hairline it wears.

radius.$description: The page's corner: a message is a box, and a box is not a pill.

padding.$description: The air above and below the message.

padding-inline.$description: The air beside the message, where it is read.

edge.$description: The ink of the hairline on every side. The tone variants recolour the leading edge alone, so this one is the quiet frame around them.

field.$description: The field's own decisions: its corner and the ink of its edge.

border.$description: The line a finger has to find: one step stronger than the dividers around it, or the control is not a control.

stat.$description: The stat's own decisions: the number it shows, and how that number is set.

value-size.$description: The size of the number: the large step of the type scale, because the number is the point of the stat.

value-weight.$description: The weight of the number: enough to be read at a glance, not enough to shout.

value-family.$description: The face the number is set in: the mono, because a figure is a figure and the mono is the face that carries figures.

table.$description: The table's own decisions: the weight of a column's heading, the ink of the rule under a row, and the fill a striped row wears.

header-weight.$description: The weight of a heading: heavier than the row beneath it, so the column names itself.

rule.$description: The ink of the rule under a row: the page's hairline.

zebra.$description: The fill a striped row wears: one step below the page, so a reader can hold their place across a wide table.

link.$description: The link's own decisions: the rule under it.

underline.$description: One pixel at the body size: the terminal underlines once, plainly.
